scores.evidence: Minimal and fixed now (changing them forces every installation to re-approve): `issues:write`, `pull_requests:write`, `contents:write` (agent branches only, enforced by rulesets)
scores.rationale: Mechanisms are mostly accurate (HMAC, SKIP LOCKED, gVisor, installation tokens, rulesets), with minor imprecision such as idempotency key semantics with delivery_id and contents:write being repo-wide while scoped only by rulesets.

scores.evidence: for issues a maintainer approves, writes a fix in a sandbox and opens a draft PR for human review.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolve with a maintainer gate, sensible scoping, and explicit deferrals each with a reason and pull-forward trigger.

scores.evidence: The sandbox runner is a separate service only because it is a security boundary, not for scaling.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, ledger ownership, and choices are applied consistently across phases, the decision table and cross-cutting table.

scores.evidence: Replaying the same delivery 10 times produces exactly one action. An injection test suite (40 or more known payloads...)
scores.rationale: Risk-specific exit checks at each phase, frozen eval sets, shadow mode, red-team sandbox tests, and ongoing regression gates and autonomy demotion, though some thresholds are unjustified but labeled as starting numbers.

scores.evidence: These are starting numbers to tune from Phase 3 and 5 data.
scores.rationale: Revisit triggers are given for each decision and numbers are labeled provisional, but scale, team size and repo size assumptions are not stated explicitly and many thresholds are invented.

scores.evidence: The design assumes injections will sometimes get through and limits what they can do: no `workflows` permission, no secrets in the sandbox, no merge rights.
scores.rationale: Covers injection, duplicates, missed webhooks, sandbox escape, runaway loops, memory poisoning, security-report leakage, re-index failure and model failure with concrete handling.

scores.evidence: Terraform for all infrastructure. The container image is built in CI and pinned by digest. Promotion is a single command.
scores.rationale: Good signals, alerts, kill switch, rollback of config, but on-call ownership, DB migration and incident response are thin.

scores.evidence: Resolve | ≤ $3, ≤ 40 tool calls, ≤ 20 min wall clock | Per repo | ≤ $50 per day
scores.rationale: Per-task, per-repo and per-org caps, routing to cheaper models and build-vs-buy triggers, but no overall run-cost estimate or engineering effort estimate.

scores.evidence: Freeze the GitHub App permission set and the installation/tenant schema. Changing either later means every installation re-approves.
scores.rationale: Identifies one-way doors (permissions, tenant schema, ledger contract, embedding versions), front-loads them, and isolates model, inner loop and sandbox behind interfaces with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith (one deployable: webhook intake, worker, policy engine).
scores.rationale: Starts simple with Postgres queue and single agent and defers much, though the eight phases, routing, and extensive eval infrastructure are somewhat heavy.

scores.evidence: The one real request: someone opens an issue in a private test repo... within 60 s the GitHub App applies one label
scores.rationale: Concrete thin first slice, dependency-ordered phases with checkable exit criteria and fallbacks, and adaptation triggers.

checklist.evidence: Autonomous | Reads, labels from the allow-list, project-board moves ... Never | Force-push, workflow edits, touching secrets
No `workflows`, `administration` or `secrets` permissions. The App is not a branch-protection bypass actor.
Every action is checked against the allow-list and validated before it runs.
gVisor, no IAM, no secrets, a read-only base image, egress proxy with an allow-list, CPU/memory/disk/time limits.
includes evidence that the test failed before the fix and passes after; diff scanner flags... extra CODEOWNER review
a triage set (≥ 500 closed issues with final labels and known duplicates); Label precision ≥ 90% on the held-out set.
Outcome capture: label corrections, PR merged/closed/edited diff... drops back automatically below 90%.
Kill switch (a flag in Postgres checked before every write)... Revise on review feedback. Capped at 2 rounds
Resolve | ≤ $3, ≤ 40 tool calls, ≤ 20 min wall clock ... Cost per merged PR drops ≥ 30%
Every run can be replayed from its ledger record.
Incremental re-index on push to the default branch. Hybrid search: BM25 plus embeddings, with re-ranking.
Replaying the same delivery 10 times produces exactly one action; an issue comment or PR review can restart the loop

traps.evidence: The App cannot bypass branch protection, so it can never merge.
no IAM, no secrets, a read-only base image, egress proxy with an allow-list
treated as *data* inside delimited blocks, never as instructions.
Cost per merged PR drops ≥ 30% with merge rate within 2 points of before.
a deliberately looping run is cut off at the cap and emits `budget_exceeded{scope}`.

note: Very strong, safety-first plan with a concrete first slice, defense-in-depth against injection, and well-gated autonomy. Weaknesses are mainly unstated scale/team assumptions, thin incident ownership, and arbitrary thresholds.
